name: Compromised web server calling out over HTTPS
description: Second lab rule for the CTIA webshell-iis-001 scenario, and the second half of the alert: three minutes after the last web-shell command, the same server opened outbound HTTPS to a single unfamiliar external address, and then again six minutes later. Small payloads on port 443, twice, to the same destination, in that order - a beacon home to a controller, not ordinary web traffic. It is scoped to the compromised host on purpose so the result is unambiguous and so it matches the last query of the investigation exactly: the alert count and the Documents count have to be the same number, or one of them is wrong. Left without a threshold so each of the two connections arrives as its own alert. A production rule would instead be a threshold query over any server making outbound connections to a destination it has no reason to call, run on a short window, with the destination list fed by a threat feed; the long time window here is a lab-only concession because this lab ships historical data from September 2026.
